findings.text: the positive control says the test "fails naming exactly PLAN-FORMAT.md:321, PLAN-FORMAT.md:330 and skills/reckon-build/references/sprint-orchestration.md:1011", but §5's test corpus is `skills/**/*.md`, which also contains `reckon crew census` at skills/reckon-build/references/orchestrator-harness/claude-code.md:266 (an identical sentence: "`reckon crew census` replaces the recipe when it lands") and a line-split `reckon migrate-project-state` at skills/reckon-sync/SKILL.md:50, so the test fails naming two more citations than the control allows

— §5 restates the health review's "261 citations … three name commands that do not exist", but that figure comes from an extractor whose corpus is the non-recursive glob `skills/reckon-*/references/*.md` (health-skill-drift/extract_commands.py:30), which skips references/orchestrator-harness/ and misses a citation split across a newline, while §5's own test uses the recursive `skills/**/*.md`; the plan builds a control on a count its cited evidence cannot support, and the review's report even flags the harness-file census sentence only indirectly via the neighbouring artifact render.py:373 → WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the wrong count sets the positive control's expectation, so the node measures against a number the evidence never established; correcting it to the real corpus size changes the done-when the node is dispatched with.
